statement: A URL/resource identity is distinct from a capture at a particular time and from the bytes returned by that capture.
actakit_implication: Source -> Acquisition -> Artifact remains a correct minimal boundary.

statement: Legal-document standards repeatedly separate abstract/document identity from version/content and physical format.
actakit_implication: Keep CivicDocument separate from Representation and Artifact.

statement: A relationship should become a first-class association/event when the relationship itself has role, time, percentage, amount or other attributes.
actakit_implication: Add an explicit future promotion rule; do not force rich relations into ClaimRelation payload JSON.

statement: Atomizing all knowledge into property/value statements gives strong machine structure but can make human-verifiable propositions unwieldy.
actakit_implication: Keep Claim as a readable proposition; structured fields are auxiliary, not its replacement.

statement: Entity reconciliation should preserve the raw source mention independently from the resolved canonical entity.
actakit_implication: Introduce/fixture EntityMention or equivalent unresolved-mention record before SQL.

statement: Mature document systems keep source files distinct from OCR/annotations/derived modifications.
actakit_implication: Original artifact remains custody object; claims/annotations/representations live separately.

statement: Document typing is useful but should be optional when it adds no value; tags/templates can carry local structure.
actakit_implication: Unknown/other is normal; profiles opt in to stronger semantics.

statement: Bulk operations are normal operator workflow in mature tools.
actakit_implication: Batch/supervised review is a 1.0 capability, without requiring ReviewBatch as canonical entity.

statement: A useful evidence citation should reopen the exact page/region/context, not merely name a document.
actakit_implication: Mesa de control should navigate from claim to source context directly.

statement: SQLite can support recursive relation traversal, FTS, filtering and broad read-only query workloads.
actakit_implication: SQLite remains justified baseline; no graph/search server required initially.

statement: Spatial/temporal/page targeting and OCR coordinate models already exist and align with Web Annotation.
actakit_implication: Use adapters/mappings for IIIF/ALTO where sources provide them; do not invent competing coordinate semantics.

statement: Heuristic segmentation can look plausible while producing contaminated or incorrect document units.
actakit_implication: Document segmentation/profile parsing needs evidence-backed correctness fixtures and fail-loud behavior.

statement: Evidence provenance should support reevaluation when processing improves.
actakit_implication: Representation/process lineage must remain queryable enough to rerun extraction without rewriting source history.

statement: Graph-shaped semantics do not require graph-optimized storage when traversal is bounded.
actakit_implication: Keep ClaimRelation explicit and bounded; graph DB is horizon only if measured workloads demand it.

statement: Simple direct relation and rich relation-object are complementary patterns, not competing universal models.
actakit_implication: Use ClaimRelation for simple proposition links; promote rich relation when relation carries independent civic meaning.

statement: Unresolved identity is legitimate data, not an ingestion failure.
actakit_implication: Allow raw mentions with no entity_id and later reconciliation.

statement: Operational observation state should not be interpreted as civic truth about absence.
actakit_implication: A failed/missing acquisition observation never deletes or negates prior records.

statement: One local canonical store plus read-only projections is operationally proven at scales well above a canton.
actakit_implication: Keep one SQLite authority and disposable FTS/read/output projections.

statement: Interoperability can be expressed at boundaries without making the internal store speak every external standard.
actakit_implication: Define mappings/export profiles; keep internal model small.

statement: The external ecosystem offers several graph/ontology/document models, none of which is a clean wholesale fit for ActaKit.
actakit_implication: ActaKit should be standards-informed, not standards-stacked.

statement: A 1–2 operator workflow benefits more from bulk review, search, reopen-source, and correction than enterprise role hierarchies.
actakit_implication: Single-operator-first remains correct.

statement: Processing can be rerun independently from document identity and original custody.
actakit_implication: Process provenance should not make a new CivicDocument every time OCR/model changes.

statement: Repeated observations of identical content are meaningful even when no new bytes need to be stored.
actakit_implication: Each successful capture keeps its own Artifact custody identity while equal content may reuse one physical ArchiveObject.

statement: Internal preservation layout and external transfer package solve different problems.
actakit_implication: Do not force BagIt/OCFL as the SQLite domain model.

statement: Bulk review can preserve per-record provenance without a permanent batch object.
actakit_implication: One command/action may write many individual review decisions atomically.

statement: Parser success is not semantic correctness.
actakit_implication: Test exact fixtures and expected structured outputs, not only no-exception/valid-schema.

statement: Physical content identity and acquisition/custody identity answer different questions even when byte deduplication is desirable.
actakit_implication: Separate ArchiveObject content-addressed bytes from per-acquisition Artifact custody identity.

statement: A defensible purge spans canonical/derived records, SQLite free-page behavior, FTS shadow indexes, archive bytes and declared backup scope rather than one DELETE operation.
actakit_implication: Freeze exact purge targets and report erasure boundaries explicitly; never equate logical deletion with corpus-wide physical erasure.
